target_offering: Builds and sells single-family detached and attached homes, mainly to individual homebuyers, across many US markets. Also develops residential lots, builds rental communities, and offers mortgage and title services through subsidiaries.
comp_offering: Designs, builds and sells single-family homes, townhomes and condominiums, mainly to first-time, move-up and active adult buyers. Homes are built on company-acquired land using subcontracted trades, and customers can personalize them at design studios. Also offers mortgage and title services through affiliates.
target_customers: B2C: individual homebuyers, including entry-level and move-up buyers; B2B: lot buyers, builders and institutional investors in rental communities
comp_customers: B2C: first-time, move-up and active adult homebuyers
notes_barbara: New homes compete; customization and land strategy differ.
notes_terra: Both companies design/build and sell new single-family and attached homes to first-time and move-up individual homebuyers. Both principally earn revenue by selling homes as homebuilders at the same point in the residential construction chain.

notes_matthew: Diamond Hill manages mutual funds and separate accounts for institutions, advisors and individuals and earns fees on assets, the same model as Cohen & Steers with a different strategy focus.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides active, valuation-driven investment management to institutions, intermediaries and individual investors. It manages mutual funds, separate accounts and private funds, and also offers fund administration and model portfolio services.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: institutions, pension plans, endowments, foundations, financial intermediaries and advisors; B2C: individual investors, including high-net-worth clients, via funds and advisors
notes_barbara: Active investment funds/accounts overlap for similar investors. Business match, but Diamond Hill was acquired by First Eagle in April 2026 and is no longer an independent listed comp.
notes_terra: Both are investment managers offering funds and separately managed accounts to institutional investors, advisors, and individuals. Each earns asset-management fees and operates at the investment-management service step.

notes_matthew: AMG's affiliates manage funds and separate accounts for the same pension funds, intermediaries and individuals that Cohen & Steers serves, and AMG's revenue is their management fees. AMG itself is a holding company over those boutiques.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Holds majority equity stakes in a group of independent boutique investment management firms and provides them with strategic, distribution and operational support. Those affiliates manage investment strategies for institutional investors, financial intermediaries and individuals, and earn fees on assets managed.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, endowments, foundations, sovereign wealth funds, and financial intermediaries; B2C: individual and high-net-worth investors via funds and managed accounts
notes_barbara: AMG’s affiliates provide investment-management products to investor clients. Owning affiliates does not move the underlying management service to a different chain step.
notes_terra: Both are investment-management businesses offering managed investment strategies and funds to institutional, intermediary, and individual investors. Both primarily earn asset-management fees and operate at the investment-adviser/manager step.

notes_matthew: WisdomTree sponsors ETFs sold through advisors and institutions and earns fees on assets. Cohen & Steers also sells ETFs and funds through the same advisor and institutional channels.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Sponsors and manages exchange-traded products (ETPs) including equity, fixed income, commodity and crypto ETFs and ETNs. Sells to investors through financial advisers, brokers and institutions. Also offers digital asset tokenization and fund services, earning fees on assets under management.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: financial advisers, broker-dealers, wealth managers, institutional investors; B2C: retail investors buying ETPs via brokerage accounts and WisdomTree digital app users
notes_barbara: Both offer investment funds/portfolios for investor allocation decisions. Active versus rules-based strategies affect fit, not the existence of an investment-management product.
notes_terra: Both are investment managers/sponsors offering pooled investment products and separate investment solutions. They serve overlapping advisers, wealth managers, institutions and retail investors and primarily earn asset-based management fees.

notes_matthew: Virtus runs mutual funds, ETFs and separate accounts for advisors, individuals and institutions and earns asset-based fees, the same business as Cohen & Steers through affiliated boutiques.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides investment management products and services through affiliated boutique managers. Serves individual investors via retail separate accounts, mutual funds and ETFs, and institutional clients via separate accounts, plus structured products such as collateralized loan obligations. Earns fees on assets managed.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2C: individual investors via advisors, mutual funds, ETFs and retail managed accounts; B2B: institutions, pension plans, endowments, insurers, wealth managers and financial advisors
notes_barbara: Funds and managed accounts compete for the same investor mandates.
notes_terra: Both are investment managers selling managed funds, ETFs and separate accounts to institutional investors, advisors and individuals. Both primarily earn asset-management fees and operate at the same investment-management step.

notes_matthew: Silvercrest manages equity and fixed income separate accounts for endowments, foundations and wealthy families and earns fees on assets. It leans toward wealth planning for families, while Cohen & Steers sells funds and institutional mandates.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides investment management and wealth planning services to high-net-worth individuals, families, trusts, foundations, endowments and institutions. Delivers through in-house investment strategies (equity, fixed income, balanced) plus family office and financial planning services, via advisors in US offices.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2C: high-net-worth individuals and families; B2B: foundations, endowments, trusts, retirement plans and other institutions
notes_barbara: Investment mandates overlap; Silvercrest adds family-office services.
notes_terra: Cohen & Steers is a specialist real-assets investment manager, whereas Silvercrest's main business is broad wealth management and planning for high-net-worth clients and institutions, so the core investment product is not interchangeable. Institutional allocators such as endowments can hire either manager, and both earn asset-management fees as investment managers.

notes_matthew: Morningstar sells research, ratings and data subscriptions to advisors and asset managers, and manages portfolios only as a small line. Investors do not hire it to run real asset funds, and its revenue is software subscriptions rather than asset-based fees.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides independent investment research, ratings, data and analytics on funds, stocks and other securities to individual investors, financial advisors, asset managers and institutions. Also manages investment portfolios for advisors and sells credit ratings and indexes. Delivered mainly through subscription software platforms and data feeds.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: asset managers, financial advisors, wealth managers, banks, insurers, issuers and institutional investors; B2C: individual investors subscribing to research and tools
comp_sic_industry: Security and Commodity Brokers, Dealers, Exchanges, and Services
notes_barbara: Managed investment portfolios overlap one Morningstar business. Research/data subscriptions dominate Morningstar’s wider model, although its investment-management activity is at the same service stage.
notes_terra: Cohen & Steers primarily manages real-assets investment funds and accounts, while Morningstar’s main business is investment research, data and subscription software. Investment professionals and advisors can buy both, but they are different offerings and monetization models.

notes_matthew: Artisan manages active equity and credit strategies in pooled funds and separate accounts for institutions, intermediaries and individuals and earns fees on assets, the same business as Cohen & Steers.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides active investment management through autonomous investment teams running distinct equity, fixed income and alternative strategies. Serves institutional investors, financial intermediaries and individual investors through pooled funds and separate accounts.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: pension plans, endowments, foundations, sovereign wealth funds, corporations, financial intermediaries and advisors; B2C: individual investors holding mutual funds
notes_barbara: Active funds and separate accounts serve the same investors.
notes_terra: Both are investment managers selling pooled funds and separate-account investment strategies to institutions, intermediaries and individual investors. Each principally earns asset-management fees and operates at the investment-manager step.

notes_matthew: Ridgepost runs private equity, venture and private credit funds of funds, an illiquid product that Cohen & Steers' fund and ETF investors cannot swap for listed real asset strategies. The same pension funds and wealth managers allocate to both and pay asset-based fees.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Multi-strategy private markets asset manager (formerly P10) offering investors access to middle and lower middle market private equity, venture capital and private credit. It runs funds-of-funds, secondaries, co-investments, GP stakes, venture debt and direct lending, earning fees on managed capital.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: institutional investors, LPs, family offices, wealth managers, fund sponsors and portfolio companies
notes_barbara: Both offer managed investment products/mandates to investors. Listed real-assets and private-market mandates differ in strategy, but both are fee-based investment-management products.
notes_terra: Compared Cohen & Steers' real-assets and listed-alternatives investment products with Ridgepost's private-markets funds and credit strategies. The investment strategies are not the same order, but both serve institutional and wealth-management investors as fee-based asset managers.

notes_matthew: GCM Grosvenor builds private hedge fund, private equity and infrastructure portfolios for pension funds and sovereign wealth funds and earns fees on assets. Those are private vehicles, not the listed funds and separate accounts Cohen & Steers sells, though the buyers overlap.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Global alternative asset management firm that manages multi-asset-class portfolios and customized investment solutions in hedge funds, private equity, infrastructure, real estate and credit. Clients are institutional investors, such as pension funds and sovereign wealth funds, and high-net-worth individuals. It invests through funds of funds, co-investments and separately managed accounts.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, foundations, insurers and financial institutions; B2C: high-net-worth individuals through private wealth channels
comp_sic_industry: Security and Commodity Brokers, Dealers, Exchanges, and Services
notes_barbara: Alternative/real-estate allocations overlap; fund structures differ.
notes_terra: Both are investment managers offering alternative/real-asset investment portfolios through funds and separately managed accounts. They serve the same institutional allocators and earn asset-management fees at the same point in the investment-management chain.

notes_matthew: SEI runs managed portfolios and funds for institutions and advisors, the same clients Cohen & Steers serves, and both earn asset-based fees. A large part of SEI's revenue is platform technology and outsourcing rather than asset management.
target_offering: Global investment manager specializing in real assets and alternatives, including real estate securities, listed infrastructure, natural resource equities, commodities, preferred securities and multi-strategy solutions. Serves institutional and individual investors through funds and separate accounts, earning fees on assets managed.
comp_offering: Provides wealth management technology platforms, investment processing and operations outsourcing, and investment management services. Clients include banks, trust companies, wealth advisors, asset managers and institutional investors. Delivers through cloud-based software, outsourced operations and managed portfolios.
target_customers: B2B: institutional investors such as pension funds, sovereign wealth funds, endowments, wealth managers and advisors; B2C: individual investors via mutual funds, ETFs and closed-end funds
comp_customers: B2B: banks, trust institutions, wealth managers, financial advisors, asset managers; B2C: high-net-worth individuals and families served via advisors and private banks
notes_barbara: SEI offers managed portfolios/funds to institutional and individual investors. Asset-management, administration and distribution fees exceed its software/processing revenue, supporting a fee-based management comparison.
notes_terra: Cohen & Steers manages specialized real-assets investment strategies, while SEI's main business is wealth-platform technology and outsourced investment operations. Institutional investors and wealth advisers can buy from both, but SEI primarily services financial intermediaries rather than acting as the same type of specialist asset manager.

notes_matthew: Fire protection and HVAC installation is not a substitute for concrete pumping, but general contractors subcontract both trades and both firms earn service revenue from branch crews on site. APi's larger business is inspection and service for building owners.
target_offering: Provides concrete pumping services with a fleet of boom, line and placing-boom pumps to commercial, infrastructure and residential contractors in the US, UK and other markets. Also provides containerized waste removal and disposal services to industrial and construction customers. Delivers services with its own branch network, equipment and operators.
comp_offering: Provides inspection, testing, maintenance, repair and installation of fire protection, life safety, security, HVAC and elevator systems, plus specialty infrastructure services. Customers are commercial, industrial and public-sector building owners and operators. Delivered through a network of branches with field technicians and contract crews.
target_customers: B2B: general and concrete contractors in commercial, infrastructure and residential construction, industrial facilities for waste services
comp_customers: B2B: commercial and industrial building owners, property managers, general contractors, utilities; B2G: government, schools, military and public infrastructure facilities
target_business_scope: Concrete pumping and placement services + Concrete washout waste management; Temporary power and supporting site infrastructure.
notes_barbara: Fire/HVAC services do not replace operated concrete pumping.
notes_terra: BBCP provides concrete pumping and placement, whereas APi’s main business is fire/life-safety and building-system installation and service, so the product is different. General contractors can buy both companies’ field services on construction projects; both earn service revenue and operate as specialty service contractors.

notes_matthew: DXP distributes MRO products and pumps to industrial plants; it does not pump concrete and its buyers are plant maintenance staff, not contractors on job sites. It earns goods revenue as a distributor.
target_offering: Provides concrete pumping services with a fleet of boom, line and placing-boom pumps to commercial, infrastructure and residential contractors in the US, UK and other markets. Also provides containerized waste removal and disposal services to industrial and construction customers. Delivers services with its own branch network, equipment and operators.
comp_offering: Distributes maintenance, repair and operating (MRO) products and provides related services to industrial customers. Also sells pumps, water and wastewater systems, and supply chain services. Sells through branches, service centers and direct sales teams.
target_customers: B2B: general and concrete contractors in commercial, infrastructure and residential construction, industrial facilities for waste services
comp_customers: B2B: industrial, energy, construction, food and beverage and manufacturing customers; B2G: municipal water and wastewater utilities
target_business_scope: Concrete pumping and placement services + Concrete washout waste management; Temporary power and supporting site infrastructure.
notes_barbara: Buying pumps/supplies is not buying concrete placement with operators.
notes_terra: Compared BBCP's contractor-facing concrete pumping service with DXP's main MRO and equipment-distribution business. DXP may serve construction broadly, but it does not offer the same pumping service or sell to the same contractor buyers in that purchasing role.

notes_matthew: Gorman-Rupp makes water and dewatering pumps sold through distributors, so a contractor cannot order a concrete pumping job from it. Contractors do buy its pumps for site dewatering, which is the only overlap.
target_offering: Provides concrete pumping services with a fleet of boom, line and placing-boom pumps to commercial, infrastructure and residential contractors in the US, UK and other markets. Also provides containerized waste removal and disposal services to industrial and construction customers. Delivers services with its own branch network, equipment and operators.
comp_offering: Designs and manufactures pumps and pump systems for moving water, wastewater and other fluids. Sells to municipal, industrial, construction, fire protection, agriculture and OEM customers, mainly through distributors.
target_customers: B2B: general and concrete contractors in commercial, infrastructure and residential construction, industrial facilities for waste services
comp_customers: B2B: industrial companies, contractors, OEMs, distributors, utilities; B2G: municipalities for water and wastewater systems
target_business_scope: Concrete pumping and placement services + Concrete washout waste management; Temporary power and supporting site infrastructure.
notes_barbara: Water-pump manufacturing differs from operated concrete-pumping services.
notes_terra: BBCP provides contractor-operated concrete pumping and placement services, while Gorman-Rupp mainly manufactures fluid-handling pumps sold through distributors. Their contractor overlap is too broad and does not reflect the same buying need or role.

notes_matthew: EZCORP's stores sell pre-owned tools, electronics and jewelry to bargain shoppers, so a thrift shopper can buy secondhand goods there, and merchandise sales are the larger share of revenue. Pawn loan fees are the core of its profit, so the revenue mix differs.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Operates pawn stores that make collateralized pawn loans to consumers and sell pre-owned and recovered merchandise such as jewelry, electronics, tools and general goods. Customers are mainly individual consumers, served through company-owned stores in the US and Latin America.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: cash-constrained individual consumers borrowing against collateral and bargain shoppers buying used goods
notes_barbara: Used merchandise competes for bargain shoppers; pawn lending adds different economics.
notes_terra: Compared Savers' thrift retail business with EZCORP's pawn-store business. Both serve bargain shoppers for pre-owned merchandise at retail, but a thrift-store purchase is not the same main order as EZCORP's pawn lending and recovered-goods sales.

notes_matthew: Vince designs new luxury apparel and sells it through department stores and its own shops; a value shopper buying used clothes at Savers is not its buyer. Vince is a brand owner, not a secondhand retailer.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Designs and sells contemporary luxury apparel and accessories for women and men under the Vince brand. Products are made by third-party manufacturers and sold to department and specialty stores, and directly to consumers through own stores and e-commerce.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: individual consumers buying through own stores and e-commerce; B2B: department stores and specialty retailers buying wholesale
comp_sic_industry: Apparel and Other Finished Products Made From Fabrics and Similar Materials
notes_barbara: Clothing overlaps, but Vince produces new goods rather than thrift resale.
notes_terra: Savers operates thrift stores selling secondhand goods to value-seeking shoppers, while Vince's main business is branded contemporary luxury apparel. Both earn primarily by selling goods, but Vince is the brand owner/manufacturer while Savers is a secondhand retailer.

notes_matthew: Williams-Sonoma sells new premium home furnishings it designs itself, to affluent shoppers; Savers sells donated used household goods to value seekers. Both sell goods through their own stores to end consumers.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Designs and sells high-quality home furnishings, cookware, kitchen tools, furniture, decor and bedding to consumers and businesses. Products are sold through e-commerce websites, catalogs and company-owned stores under several brands. Products are mostly designed in-house and made by third-party manufacturers.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: home furnishing and kitchen shoppers, families, gift and registry customers; B2B: commercial and trade customers, hospitality and design professionals
notes_barbara: Homewares overlap; premium new furnishings differ from used-goods resale.
notes_terra: Compared Savers’ thrift retail stores with Williams-Sonoma’s main business of selling new, premium home furnishings and kitchen goods. They are both goods retailers, but the offerings and buyer segments are not interchangeable.

notes_matthew: Upbound leases new furniture and appliances to credit-constrained consumers, earning recurring lease payments, not retail sales of used goods. Both reach the household directly, but the lease-to-own buyer is solving a credit need, not shopping secondhand.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Provides lease-to-own access to furniture, appliances, electronics and computers, mainly for consumers with limited credit access. Operates Rent-A-Center stores, Acima lease-to-own through partner retailers, and the Brigit financial app. Customers make recurring payments with an option to own.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: credit-challenged consumers leasing household goods; B2B: retail partners offering lease-to-own at point of sale
notes_barbara: Budget-conscious households can obtain furniture/household goods from either company. Upbound mainly earns rental/lease-to-own fees, unlike Savers’ used-merchandise sales.
notes_terra: Savers sells secondhand apparel and household goods outright through thrift stores, while Upbound’s main business is lease-to-own financing/access for new durable goods. Their consumer segments and purchase needs differ, and Upbound earns recurring lease payments rather than retail merchandise sales.

notes_matthew: A parent buying used kids' clothes at Savers can buy new value-priced children's clothing at Carter's, so the children's apparel line overlaps. Carter's is a brand owner that designs and sources its goods and sells a large share wholesale.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Designs, sources and markets apparel, sleepwear, bedding and accessories for babies and young children under its own brands. Sells through its own retail stores and websites, wholesale customers and licensees. Products are made by third-party contract manufacturers.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: parents and gift-givers buying baby and children's clothing; B2B: department stores, mass-market retailers and international wholesale partners
comp_sic_industry: Apparel and Other Finished Products Made From Fabrics and Similar Materials
notes_barbara: Children's clothes overlap; new-brand supply differs from thrift resale.
notes_terra: Compared Savers’ for-profit secondhand-goods retailing with Carter’s branded new baby and children’s apparel business. Thrift shoppers are not the same customer segment as Carter’s parents and gift-givers buying new children’s clothing.

notes_matthew: Ingles sells groceries; Savers sells secondhand clothing and household goods. Both are store retailers selling goods to households, but the shopping need is different.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Operates supermarkets in the southeastern US that sell groceries, fresh foods, pharmacy items, fuel and general merchandise to consumers. Also owns a fluid milk processing plant and produces some private-label dairy goods, and owns and leases out shopping center real estate.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: household grocery shoppers in the southeastern US
notes_barbara: Groceries do not replace secondhand apparel or homewares.
notes_terra: Savers operates thrift stores for secondhand goods, while Ingles's main business is supermarkets selling groceries and general merchandise. Both sell goods directly to consumers, but value-seeking secondhand shoppers are not the same buying segment as household grocery shoppers.

notes_matthew: Build-A-Bear sells new plush toys made to order in its own stores to gift buyers and kids. It is a brand retailer of new goods, not a secondhand store, though both sell goods direct to consumers.
target_offering: Operates for-profit thrift stores selling secondhand clothing, accessories and household goods to value-seeking consumers. Sources donated goods from nonprofit partners and community donation centers, then processes and prices them for sale in its own stores.
comp_offering: Sells customizable plush toys that customers stuff, dress and personalize in store, plus clothing, accessories and licensed plush. Sells to families and gift buyers through its own stores, e-commerce, and franchise and wholesale partners.
target_customers: B2C: value-seeking shoppers buying secondhand apparel and household goods; B2B: wholesale buyers of unsold goods, such as graders and resellers
comp_customers: B2C: children, parents, gift buyers and collectors; B2B: franchisees, wholesale and licensing partners, commercial retail partners
notes_barbara: A comparable ready-to-buy plush/toy assortment at Savers remains unconfirmed. Build-A-Bear’s customized plush experience alone does not prove the same product and buyer purchase.
notes_terra: Savers operates thrift stores for secondhand apparel and household goods, while Build-A-Bear's main business is customizable plush toys and related merchandise. Both sell goods through retail channels, but shoppers are purchasing for different needs and cannot substitute the same order.

notes_matthew: Grand Canyon Education sells back-office, marketing and technology services to Grand Canyon University for a share of tuition; it does not enroll students. It earns service fees like APEI but sits one step behind the school instead of teaching the student.
target_offering: Operates for-profit postsecondary education institutions that deliver online and campus-based degree and certificate programs. Serves military service members, veterans, public safety professionals, nursing and healthcare students, and other adult learners. Revenue comes mainly from tuition paid by students, government tuition assistance and federal student aid.
comp_offering: Provides education services to private universities, chiefly Grand Canyon University, its largest client. Services include technology, academic and student support, marketing and enrollment support, and campus facilities, delivered under long-term contracts for a share of university revenue.
target_customers: B2C: adult students, military service members, veterans, nurses and healthcare students; B2G: military tuition assistance and federal student aid funding; B2B: employer and partner tuition arrangements
comp_customers: B2B: private, nonprofit universities, mainly Grand Canyon University, plus other partner institutions
notes_barbara: University outsourcing is upstream of selling education to students.
notes_terra: APEI directly provides postsecondary degree and certificate programs to adult students, while LOPE's main business provides outsourced education, marketing, and campus services to universities. The buyers and roles differ: students enroll with APEI, whereas universities contract with LOPE.

notes_matthew: Legacy Education runs campus-based nursing and allied health colleges; a nursing student at APEI's schools can enroll there instead. Both live on student tuition and federal aid.
target_offering: Operates for-profit postsecondary education institutions that deliver online and campus-based degree and certificate programs. Serves military service members, veterans, public safety professionals, nursing and healthcare students, and other adult learners. Revenue comes mainly from tuition paid by students, government tuition assistance and federal student aid.
comp_offering: Owns and operates post-secondary allied health colleges offering career training programs such as nursing, veterinary technology, and MRI and ultrasound technology. Serves students seeking healthcare careers, delivered through campus-based instruction at 4 schools on 6 campuses in California.
target_customers: B2C: adult students, military service members, veterans, nurses and healthcare students; B2G: military tuition assistance and federal student aid funding; B2B: employer and partner tuition arrangements
comp_customers: B2C: post-secondary students pursuing healthcare careers
notes_barbara: Nursing/allied-health training competes for student enrollments and tuition.
notes_terra: Both operate postsecondary institutions offering nursing and healthcare career programs to adult students. Each earns mainly through tuition and aid-funded education services delivered directly to students.

notes_matthew: UTI runs tuition-funded postsecondary career schools, and its Concorde campuses offer nursing and allied health programs like APEI's healthcare schools. Its core automotive and skilled trades programs do not overlap with APEI's degree offerings.
target_offering: Operates for-profit postsecondary education institutions that deliver online and campus-based degree and certificate programs. comp_customers: B2C: residential broadband subscribers; B2B: wireless carriers, enterprises, other telecom carriers, hyperscalers; B2G: federal, state and local government agencies

notes_terra: Both operate fiber networks and sell broadband plus wholesale fiber transport/connectivity. They serve the same residential, business, carrier, and government connectivity buyers through recurring telecom-service revenue.

notes_matthew: Legence installs and maintains mechanical, electrical and plumbing systems in commercial and institutional buildings with recurring service work, which overlaps APi's HVAC and building-systems service business. target_offering: Provides inspection, testing, maintenance, repair and installation of fire protection, life safety, security, HVAC and elevator systems, plus specialty infrastructure services. comp_customers: B2B: data center operators, healthcare systems, life sciences firms, universities, commercial and industrial building owners; B2G: public institutions and government facilities
notes_barbara: Mechanical/electrical installation and maintenance overlap facility-owner orders.
notes_terra: Both provide installation and recurring maintenance for building systems, including APi's HVAC/life-safety work and Legence's MEP systems. They sell field and project services to the same commercial, institutional, industrial, and public-facility owners at the same service-contractor step.

notes_matthew: Amentum runs long-term engineering, program management and operations contracts for defense, space and nuclear agencies. Both sell services delivered by their own technicians, but a building owner buying fire protection inspection from APi would not place that order with Amentum.
target_offering: Provides inspection, testing, maintenance, repair and installation of fire protection, life safety, security, HVAC and elevator systems, plus specialty infrastructure services. target_customers: B2B: commercial and industrial building owners, property managers, general contractors, utilities; B2G: government, schools, military and public infrastructure facilities
comp_customers: B2G: US Department of Defense, DOE, NASA, intelligence agencies, and allied governments; B2B: commercial energy, infrastructure and industrial clients, and prime contractors
comp_sic_industry: Engineering, Accounting, Research, Management, and Related Services

notes_terra: APi provides field installation, inspection, and maintenance of building life-safety systems, while Amentum’s main business is government engineering, program management, and technical operations. Both earn service-contract revenue and perform services, but their primary offerings and buying roles differ.

target_offering: Provides inspection, testing, maintenance, repair and installation of fire protection, life safety, security, HVAC and elevator systems, plus specialty infrastructure services. notes_terra: Both provide field-delivered inspection, testing and compliance services for critical building and infrastructure systems. They sell service work to overlapping commercial, industrial, utility and public-facility owners.

comp_customers: B2B: data center operators, general contractors, commercial and industrial owners, homebuilders, utilities, industrial manufacturers; B2C: homeowners for residential electrical and service work

notes_terra: Both provide installation and maintenance services for commercial and industrial building systems, with overlap in mechanical/HVAC-related work. They sell field-delivered contracting and service work to the same owners, operators, developers and general contractors.

comp_customers: B2B: building owners, general contractors, developers, data center and manufacturing operators, hospitals, universities; B2G: government and public institutional facilities, schools
notes_barbara: HVAC/mechanical installation and maintenance overlap APi building services.

notes_matthew: The ONE Group operates full-service restaurants and bars, so a Flanigan's diner can buy the same sit-down meal and drinks there, even if STK is more upscale. Both earn most revenue from company-operated restaurant sales.

target_customers: B2C: restaurant diners and liquor store shoppers in South Florida
comp_customers: B2C: restaurant and bar guests, diners, and event attendees; B2B: hotel owners and licensees, corporate event and private dining clients
notes_barbara: Full-service restaurants/bars compete for diners and event spending.
notes_terra: Compared Flanigan’s restaurant operations with ONE Group’s owned and operated restaurants and bars. Both sell full-service dining and drinks directly to diners, earning food-and-beverage service revenue as restaurant operators.

notes_matthew: Dutch Bros sells drive-thru coffee and energy drinks, not sit-down seafood meals or package liquor. Both are company-operated food service, but the buying occasion is different.

target_customers: B2C: restaurant diners and liquor store shoppers in South Florida
comp_customers: B2C: individual consumers buying drinks at drive-thru shops; B2B: franchisees who license the brand and buy supplies
notes_barbara: Drive-through coffee orders differ from Flanigan’s sit-down meals and bar service. A broad consumer food-and-drink audience alone does not establish the same dining purchase.
notes_terra: Compared Flanigan’s full-service restaurant and package-liquor business with Dutch Bros’ drive-thru made-to-order beverage shops. They are both consumer food-service retailers, but a Flanigan’s meal or liquor purchase is not the same order or consumer need as Dutch Bros’ main beverage business.

notes_matthew: Wendy's is a quick-service burger chain that earns most of its revenue from franchisee royalties, fees and rent. Flanigan's runs its own full-service restaurants and liquor stores, so neither the product nor the franchisor model matches.

comp_offering: Franchises and operates Wendy's quick-service restaurants selling hamburgers, chicken sandwiches, fries and breakfast to consumers through dine-in, drive-thru and digital ordering. Most restaurants are run by franchisees who pay royalties and fees; a small share is company-operated.
target_customers: B2C: restaurant diners and liquor store shoppers in South Florida
comp_customers: B2C: individual consumers dining in, drive-thru, takeout and delivery; B2B: franchisees who buy franchise rights and supplies
notes_barbara: Prepared restaurant meals overlap, but Wendy’s franchise fees/royalties differ from a restaurant operator’s meal-service revenue. The service/dining experience is narrower than a clean whole-company match.
notes_terra: Both operate restaurant brands selling prepared meals and drinks to consumer diners, albeit in different formats. Flanigan's primarily earns from company-operated restaurant and liquor-store sales, while Wendy's main business is franchising and collecting royalties and fees.

notes_matthew: Texas Roadhouse operates company-owned full-service casual dining restaurants with a bar, selling to the same families and diners Flanigan's serves. Both earn revenue from their own restaurant sales.

target_customers: B2C: restaurant diners and liquor store shoppers in South Florida
comp_customers: B2C: families and individual diners eating in or ordering takeout
notes_barbara: Both operate casual full-service restaurants serving meals/drinks.
notes_terra: Compared Flanigan's casual full-service restaurant business with Texas Roadhouse's casual dining restaurants. Both directly serve dine-in and takeout meals and drinks to individual and family diners.

Its restaurant and nightlife line is a minor part, so a Flanigan's diner is not its customer in any meaningful way, though both operate their own venues and sell services to consumers.

comp_offering: Owns and operates live entertainment venues in New York and Chicago, including Madison Square Garden, Radio City Music Hall and several theaters. notes_matthew: Ingles is a supermarket chain selling groceries. notes_barbara: Retail liquor/fuel activity overlaps a narrow part of Flanigan’s business. Ingles mainly sells grocery merchandise rather than restaurant dining services.
notes_terra: Compared Flanigan's restaurant and package-liquor retail business with Ingles's supermarket business. Restaurant dining and specialty liquor shopping are not the same consumer order or need as grocery shopping; Ingles mainly sells goods while Flanigan's main offering is food service.

comp_customers: B2C: residential households using propane for heating, cooking and water heating, grill-cylinder buyers; B2B: commercial, industrial and agricultural customers, retailers carrying tank exchange, wholesale buyers
